coverage: Sources checked for this review: the official Expo 2027 programme and calendar pages, the organiser's participants pages, and the national announcements linked on each entry. This list records what we have found. It is not a record of everything that has been announced anywhere.

entries.authority: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Trade
entries.sourceNote: Ministry of Trade procurement notice for the pavilion's design, construction and operation, published August 2026.
entries.establishes: That 19 May 2027 is the date Türkiye plans for its Expo National Day.
entries.doesNotEstablish: Programme times, venue, performers, whether events are open to general Expo visitors, or whether any part requires a separate reservation. The notice also anticipates activity on other significant days and weeks, so this is not necessarily Türkiye's only dated programme.
entries.context: 19 May is also a Turkish public holiday — Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day — marking Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's landing at Samsun on 19 May 1919, which began the War of Independence. For an Expo themed "Play for Humanity: Sport and Music for All", a day already dedicated to youth and sport is a striking fit. Nothing published explains whether that shaped the choice, and it should not be read as a rule: countries do not systematically pick their domestic national day.

undated.note: A National Day with Emirati cultural showcases is described as part of the UAE's participation. No date has been published.
undated.sourceNote: Gulf News on the UAE at Expo 2027.

precedent.note: At Expo 2025 Osaka the organiser released National Day and Special Day dates in batches rather than all at once. A release on 20 June 2024 added 31 countries to an earlier April 2024 batch, bringing the published total to 131 countries and four international organisations — roughly ten months before that Expo opened on 13 April 2025.
precedent.caution: This describes how a different Expo published its schedule. It does not establish when Expo 2027 Belgrade, or any individual country, will announce.

sources.note: Official programme page — no country-to-date National Day schedule published as of 13 Sep 2026
The calendar linked from the official programme page is labelled Playground Events, not National Days
Participants FAQ (dated December 2024) — states that participating countries can select a National Day

caveats: A date being announced by a national authority does not make it final. Where a source says "planned", we say planned.
An Expo National Day is a container for a programme. Knowing the date tells you nothing by itself about times, access or whether a reservation is needed.
Coverage will be uneven: well-resourced delegations announce earlier and more publicly. A country missing from this list has not necessarily done less.

history.change: First publication. One dated entry (Türkiye), one undated announcement (UAE).
